metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Hong Kong (China)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Hong Kong (China) using OECD’s published PISA 2022 database tables (e.g., III.B1.2.1, III.B1.4.3, III.B1.5.*). The document does not specify the exact student weight variable names or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied in the production of these estimates. For analysts working with PISA microdata, the standard approach is to use the provided sampling weights to obtain population-representative estimates and to apply the corresponding replicate weights (if available) for uncertainty quantification under the complex survey design. Because this is a published results factsheet rather than a re-analysis paper, the specific weighting implementation details are not documented here; users should follow the PISA 2022 technical documentation for the correct weight and variance-estimation procedure.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and related associations; it does not report an analysis pipeline that imputes or combines plausible values (PVs) for a student-level predictive model. The reported outcomes are presented as OECD estimates (means, proficiency shares, correlations, and explained variance) derived from the PISA 2022 database tables, but the factsheet does not document PV combination rules or missing-data handling steps. Therefore, missing-data handling is treated as not reported for this extraction because the methodological details are not provided in the factsheet text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Hong Kong (China) results for the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test. It states that 5,907 students in 163 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 48,200 15-year-olds (about 81% of the total 15-year-old population in Hong Kong (China)). The factsheet does not describe additional analytic exclusions (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds or missing background questionnaire rules), so the extraction records the stated completed-assessment subset as the analytic basis.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 creative thinking results for 15-year-old students in Hong Kong (China). The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Hong Kong (China) has a mean creative thinking score of 32/60, which is statistically significantly lower than the OECD average (33). About 77% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), while 22% are top performers at Levels 5–6. The factsheet also reports that mathematics performance is strongly associated with creative thinking within Hong Kong (China) (correlation 0.63; 29% of variance uniquely attributed to mathematics), and it documents within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender, plus patterns in ideation-process and domain-context relative success. It is descriptive and does not provide an ML modeling evaluation or causal identification strategy.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (descriptive reporting) rather than an empirical ML study. As such, there is no student-level predictive modeling, no explicit PV-combination or missing-data imputation strategy described in the text, and no ML algorithms or performance metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) are evaluated. The extraction therefore leaves ML-related fields empty and focuses on the reported PISA 2022 creative thinking benchmarks and associations.
